title: Add heuristics: AlphaSAGE GFlowNet diversity, SubjECTive-QA validated taxonomy
rationale: Two generalizable lessons from tonight's dream cycle scan: (1) GFlowNet-based alpha generators produce more diverse, uncorrelated alphas than pure RL approaches because they optimize for a distribution of good solutions rather than a single optimum — relevant whenever building alpha libraries. (2) When designing LLM scoring dimensions for earnings call analysis, prefer validated taxonomies with public benchmark datasets (like SubjECTive-QA) over ad-hoc prompt engineering — they transfer better and can be calibrated against ground truth annotations.
content:
### GFlowNet diversity advantage for alpha mining
- LESSON: GFlowNet-based alpha generators (AlphaSAGE) produce more diverse, uncorrelated factors than RL-based generators (AlphaGen-PPO) because they sample proportional to reward rather than argmax — avoid mode collapse
- WHEN: Building alpha libraries for R33 or any factor mining task; use GFlowNet generators to fill uncorrelated niches that RL-based generators miss
- SOURCE: arXiv:2509.25055 (AlphaSAGE), 2026-04-25 dream cycle

### Prefer validated scoring taxonomies over ad-hoc LLM prompts
- LESSON: For multi-dimension text scoring tasks (earnings call quality, analyst evasion), prefer taxonomies with public annotated datasets and benchmark F1 scores over designing dimensions from scratch — they transfer better, can be calibrated, and don't require justification to stakeholders
- WHEN: Any new LLM scoring dimension for R28/R31/R29 — first check if a validated public dataset (SubjECTive-QA, FinQA, etc.) covers the construct before designing novel prompts
- SOURCE: arXiv:2410.20651 (SubjECTive-QA NeurIPS 2024), 2026-04-25 dream cycle
